original:
Matthew 26:39 has Christ going "a little farther" in Gethsemane, falling on His face, and praying. Even He went a little farther. Father, I keep stopping short. I pray for two minutes and call it good. I take the conversation about the marriage right up to the hard part and then change the subject. I confess the comfortable sin and skip the uncomfortable one. Help me go a little farther today. Not all the way to the bloody-sweat extreme of Christ. Just a little farther than I would have on my own. Five more minutes in prayer. One more honest sentence with my wife. One more name on my intercession list. Christ went farther for me. I can go a little farther for the people in my life.

Amen.
rewritten:
Father, Matthew 26 shows Jesus going a little farther in Gethsemane and praying. I keep stopping short.

I pray briefly and call it enough. I bring the hard conversation close to honesty and then change the subject. I confess the comfortable sin and leave the deeper one unnamed. Help me go a little farther today, not as a performance, and not to imitate what only Christ could bear, but because Christ has already gone farther for me.

Give me five more honest minutes in prayer. Give me one more truthful sentence with my wife. Give me one more name to carry before You instead of one more excuse to stay busy.

Make the next step plain, and give me enough courage to take it.

Amen.
